outputs.without:
1. Deploy an idempotency store (keyed by `campaign_id + subscriber_id`) checked atomically by all newsletter workers before handing any email payload to the mail transfer agent.
2. Drain and pause new campaign dispatches briefly or fence legacy queue publishers so each campaign batch is assigned exclusively to either the old queue or the upgraded queue, never both.
3. Stand up the upgraded queue consumers in parallel to process newly enqueued campaigns while old workers finish draining remaining in-flight messages from the legacy queue.
4. Decommission the legacy queue only after its depth and unacknowledged-message counts remain at 0 for 30 minutes and deduplication logs show clean handoff.

Rollback Trigger: Idempotency guard detects more than 0 duplicate send attempts per campaign, or dead-letter queue growth exceeds 1% of enqueued messages within 5 minutes.

Smoke Check: Enqueue a test campaign to an internal seed list, simulate a worker redelivery of the same message ID, and confirm exactly one email arrives per recipient.
outputs.with:
1. Validate idempotent message deduplication keys and consumer locking in staging by replaying duplicate queue deliveries and confirming each subscriber receives at most one newsletter send.
2. Deploy the upgraded newsletter queue consumers to production with traffic routing OFF, verify health endpoints and dead-letter monitoring, and confirm old queue drainage before switching producers.
3. Route 5% of newsletter dispatches through the upgraded queue with a shared deduplication ledger active across both old and new workers, monitoring send counts and queue lag for 24 hours.
4. Gradually shift 25%, 50%, and 100% of newsletter sends to the new queue while auditing send-receipt logs, then decommission the legacy queue after a 1-week zero-duplicate soak.

**Rollback trigger:** Halt producers and disable the new-queue routing flag immediately if duplicate send count > 0 (any `send_count > 1` for a `(campaign_id, subscriber_id)` pair) or delivery error rate exceeds 2x baseline.

**Smoke check:** Enqueue a test newsletter campaign for an internal test list in staging/canary, deliberately replay the same job payload once, and verify the mail-sink log records exactly one delivered message per recipient with exit status 0.

blind: B is more rigorous because it validates deduplication in staging, verifies inactive consumers and old queue drainage before switching producers, canaries at 5% for 24 hours before ramping 25%-100%, and triggers producer/routing halt on any actual duplicate send.
